paragraphs.text: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia-2 (CAMT2) is an autosomal recessive disorder. Affected children have severe thrombocytopenia with reduced or absent bone marrow megakaryocytes. Some also have anemia and/or neutropenia, and the disease can progress to trilineage bone marrow aplasia in childhood (Pecci et al., 2018; Capaci et al., 2023). Because the defect lies in the cytokine thrombopoietin and not in hematopoietic cells, serum THPO levels are not raised as expected. Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is ineffective, but patients respond to THPO-receptor agonists (Seo et al., 2017; Pecci et al., 2018; Capaci et al., 2023).

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) reported 3 affected sibs born to Egyptian parents who were first cousins. The proband, a boy, presented at age 3.5 years with ecchymotic patches. He had very severe thrombocytopenia (platelet count 3 x 10(9)/l), hyporegenerative anemia (reticulocyte count 22.8 x 10(9)/l) and severe neutropenia (0.3 x 10(9)/l). Platelet size was normal and there were no cytomorphologic abnormalities. Bone marrow was hypocellular with very rare immature megakaryocytes, and the marrow karyotype was normal. Fanconi anemia and paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria were excluded, and he was diagnosed with idiopathic aplastic anemia. He then had recurrent major hemorrhages (epistaxis, gum bleeding and rectal bleeding) and recurrent severe infections, which required multiple platelet and red blood cell transfusions. On examination he also had preauricular skin tags and a left divergent squint. His brother had severe isolated thrombocytopenia (26 x 10(9)/l) at age 7 months, with a markedly decreased number of bone marrow megakaryocytes. From age 1.6 years he had recurrent spontaneous bleeding that required platelet transfusions. A younger sister developed a hematoma at a vaccination site at age 2 months and was found to have anemia and severe thrombocytopenia. The parents had normal blood counts. Thrombocytopenia was the only feature present in all 3 patients. The authors suggested that the trilineage aplasia in the oldest sib meant that the hematologic picture worsens with age. They considered the presentation indistinguishable from that of CAMT due to MPL mutations.

paragraphs.text: Capaci et al. (2023) reported a boy born to Muslim Palestinian parents who were first cousins. He presented at age 3.5 years with easy bruising and thrombocytopenia (platelet count 21 x 10(9)/L), with a normal mean platelet volume. His platelet count shortly after birth had been 70 x 10(9)/L. At age 2 years it was 20 x 10(9)/L, when he was diagnosed with urethral stenosis and received a platelet transfusion before meatotomy. Apart from occasional mild neutropenia he had no other cytopenias. Two bone marrow biopsies showed normocellular marrow with severe megakaryocyte hypoplasia, a few small immature forms, and mild dyserythropoiesis. Chromosome breakage analysis ruled out Fanconi anemia, and the bone marrow karyotype was normal (46,XY). He did not have pancytopenia. The authors hypothesized that, without treatment, he would have progressed to multilineage marrow aplasia.

The authors therefore considered these levels inappropriately low, consistent with defective THPO production.

paragraphs.text: Dasouki et al. (2013) studied 2 Micronesian sibs with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia. By whole-exome sequencing, they identified a homozygous c.112C-T missense mutation in the THPO gene that results in an arg38-to-cys substitution (R17C when the 21-residue signal peptide is excluded) in the receptor-binding domain. In silico modeling predicted that this fifth cysteine could disrupt normal disulfide bonding and impair receptor binding. In functional assays, medium containing mutant THPO was 2- to 3-fold less able to sustain proliferation of THPO-dependent UT7-TPO cells. Both parents and a sib were heterozygous and had reduced platelet counts, and a sib with wildtype sequence had a normal platelet count. The authors concluded that this partial loss-of-function allele causes aplastic anemia in the homozygous state and mild thrombocytopenia in the heterozygous state.

paragraphs.text: In the proband of an Egyptian family with CAMT, Pecci et al. (2018) sequenced MPL and THPO. They found no MPL variant but identified a homozygous c.355C-T transition in the THPO gene, resulting in an arg119-to-cys (R119C) substitution. The 2 affected sibs were also homozygous and the parents were heterozygous. The variant was absent from the SNP, 1000 Genomes, and ExAC databases. The residue lies in helix C of the MPL-binding domain and is highly conserved, including in EPO. In HEK293T cells, the mutant protein was expressed and stable, but its concentration in culture supernatants was about 23-fold lower than wildtype. At equal THPO concentrations, the mutant retained about 50% of wildtype activity in stimulating UT7-TPO cell proliferation and showed defective activation of STAT5, ERK1/2, and AKT. The previously reported R38C variant behaved similarly.

paragraphs.text: Capaci et al. (2023) studied a Palestinian boy with CAMT. By whole-exome sequencing, they identified a homozygous c.-323C-T substitution in the promoter region of the THPO gene, 45 nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site of transcript variant 1. Both parents and a younger sib were heterozygous, and 2 healthy sibs were homozygous for the wildtype allele. The variant was listed in dbSNP but was absent from gnomAD, and it lies in a region conserved across species. No variants were found in MPL, MECOM, HOXA11, RBM8A, or genes associated with Fanconi anemia or other inherited bone marrow failure syndromes. The variant was predicted to abolish consensus binding sites for ETS1 and STAT4. In HEK293T cells it reduced THPO promoter-driven luciferase reporter activity by almost 80%, and in chromatin immunoprecipitation assays binding to the promoter was impaired, at least for STAT4.

paragraphs.text: Pecci et al. (2018) treated all 3 affected sibs with romiplostim. The proband had not responded to cyclosporine A or oxymetholone. At age 4.4 years he started romiplostim at 1 microgram/kg/week for 3 months, followed by 4 micrograms/kg monthly, and had a rapid trilineage response. His mean neutrophil count rose from 0.7 to 1.7 x 10(9)/l. He had no further spontaneous bleeding, infections, or transfusions during 6.5 years of follow-up. His brother achieved a platelet response, remission of bleeding, and transfusion independence over 6.3 years of follow-up. His sister had platelet and hemoglobin responses. No side effects attributable to romiplostim were observed.

checks.evidence_quote: The analysis confirmed that both p.R119C and p.R38C THPO induce defective activation of all the investigated intracellular signaling kinases
checks.explanation: Kinases were STAT5, ERK1/2 and AKT in UT7-TPO cells.

checks.claim: Serum THPO levels in the patients homozygous for THPO R119C were within the normal range.
checks.evidence_quote: Thrombopoietin levels measured in the sera of the two older siblings collected before romiplostim administration were within the normal range.
checks.explanation: Only the two older siblings were measured; the sister's level is not reported.

paragraphs.text: Capaci et al. (2023) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous c.-323C-T substitution in the THPO promoter region in a Palestinian boy with CAMT born to consanguineous parents. Both parents and a younger sib were heterozygous, and the heterozygous mother had mild thrombocytopenia. The variant abolished predicted ETS1 and STAT4 binding sites and reduced promoter-driven luciferase reporter activity by almost 80% in HEK293T cells. In chromatin immunoprecipitation assays, transcription factor binding to the mutant promoter was impaired.

checks.claim: Capaci et al. (2023) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous c.-323C-T substitution in the THPO promoter region.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole exome sequencing analysis revealed a homozygous (c.-323C>T) substitution in a potentially regulatory region of the THPO gene

checks.claim: The homozygous THPO c.-323C-T promoter variant was found in a Palestinian boy with CAMT.
checks.evidence_quote: In a child with the clinical picture of CAMT, we identified the homozygous c.-323C>T substitution, affecting a potential regulatory region of THPO.
checks.explanation: The child is a boy of Palestinian parents.

checks.claim: The Palestinian boy with CAMT homozygous for THPO c.-323C-T was born to consanguineous parents.
checks.evidence_quote: The proband was born to Muslim Palestinian parents who are first cousins to one another.

checks.claim: Both parents and a younger sib of the Palestinian boy were heterozygous for THPO c.-323C-T.
checks.evidence_quote: segregation analysis revealed that the parents and the younger sibling of the proband (II-4) were heterozygous for c.-323C>T

checks.claim: The mother, heterozygous for THPO c.-323C-T, had mild thrombocytopenia.
checks.evidence_quote: His mother (I-2) has a history of mild thrombocytopenia that worsened during each pregnancy; her platelet counts are now stable around 80x109/L

checks.claim: The THPO c.-323C-T variant abolished predicted ETS1 and STAT4 binding sites.
checks.evidence_quote: Of note, these putative binding sites were not recognized when the c.-323C>T substitution was included in a query sequence.
checks.explanation: The predicted ETS1 and STAT4 sites are lost with the variant.

checks.claim: The THPO c.-323C-T variant reduced promoter-driven luciferase reporter activity by almost 80% in HEK293T cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Transfecting HEK293T cells, which constitutively express THPO, we observed that c.-323C>T significantly reduced (by almost 80%) the reporter activity

checks.claim: In chromatin immunoprecipitation assays, transcription factor binding to the THPO c.-323C-T mutant promoter was impaired.
checks.evidence_quote: Binding of the transcription factors to the mutant promoter was lower, though with different affinity (Figure 2D).
